en: Itivuttaka 4: Ekakanipāta, First Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Accomplished One, it was so stated by the Well-Gone One. Regarding this, the meaning is as follows: “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? It is unwholesome covetousness. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? It is wholesome non-covetousness. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The same formula is repeated for the following pairs: Unwholesome ill-will / Wholesome non-ill-will Unwholesome sloth and torpor / Wholesome non-sloth and non-torpor Unwholesome restlessness and remorse / Wholesome non-restlessness and non-remorse Unwholesome doubt / Wholesome non-doubt Unwholesome lack of faith / Wholesome faith Unwholesome lack of moral shame / Wholesome moral shame Unwholesome lack of moral dread / Wholesome moral dread Unwholesome lack of learning / Wholesome learning Unwholesome lack of energy / Wholesome energy Unwholesome lack of wisdom / Wholesome wisdom “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time.

What is that one thing? It is unwholesome lack of wisdom. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? It is wholesome wisdom. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Accomplished One, it was so stated by the Well-Gone One. Regarding this, the meaning is as follows. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!”—“Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? It is unwholesome wrong view. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. “Monks, there is one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? It is wholesome right view. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
I am your guarantor for non-returning.
Abandon anger, monks; that is the one thing.
This is what the Blessed One said.
“Having fully understood that anger by which beings, when angry, go to an evil destination— ”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
